publication.prior_report_citation: [13–20] (Patients 2–12 in Table 1 are previously reported cases; Patient 1 is the current report)

individuals.treatment_summary: Antibiotics (amoxicillin/potassium clavulanate followed by cefotaxime for two weeks) without immediate effect on fever; hemoglobin infusions (Fig. 1b); ganciclovir for two weeks for CMV; no immunosuppressive treatment.
individuals.clinical_diagnosis_basis: Metagenomic next generation sequencing prompted genomic deletions; comparative genomic hybridization array revealed a heterozygous 5.15 Mb deletion in 6q23.3q24.3 affecting at least 30 genes including TNFAIP3; then definitively diagnosed with HA20.

phenotypic_features.feature_text_as_stated: preterm (delivered, at a gestational age of 36 weeks, by cesarean section)
phenotypic_features.severity_or_detail: born via in vitro fertilization; birth weight 2700 g

phenotypic_features.feature_text_as_stated: recurrent episodes of low to moderate-grade fever
phenotypic_features.severity_or_detail: 37.6–39℃, one to three times per day; did not subside with antibiotics; resolved gradually within 24 days; another slight fever lasting about one week later; listed as initial symptom (Table 1)
4 cm below the right costal margin on admission; ameliorated at six months (3 cm below the right costal margin); Table 1 Hepatomegaly +; abdominal ultrasonography showed hepatomegaly
2.5 cm below the left costal margin on admission; not palpable at six months; Table 1 Splenomegaly +

phenotypic_features.feature_text_as_stated: slightly elevated white blood cell counts

phenotypic_features.severity_or_detail: gradually returned to normal levels accompanied by extinguished fever within 22 days
worsened gradually after onset of fever; hemoglobin infusions (Fig. 1b); mild anemia reappeared after another slight fever; Table 1 Anemia +
constantly for 10 days after onset of the febrile attacks (ALT, AST; Fig. 1c); hepatic injury reappeared after another slight fever; Table 1 Hepatic dysfunction +; described as liver injury
metagenomic next generation sequencing CMV positive; PCR detected CMV DNA in serum; treated with ganciclovir for two weeks
no clear evidence of hemoglobin loss or hemolysis
without clinical signs of active bleeding

phenotypic_features.feature_text_as_stated: routine test of urine, feces and kidney function were normal

phenotypic_features.severity_or_detail: negative; hemoglobin analysis, red cell osmotic fragility test and enzymatic activity test of G6PD also negative
authors state anemia caused by iron deficiency and AIHA reported in HA20 'was not in accordance with our patient'
No other obvious abnormalities were found
